title: Talk it through 1.2
role: Event coordinator briefing a colleague on what is certain and what is not
can_do: I can say how sure I am about a plan or an event.
I can use likely, probable and certain in clear, precise sentences.

nodes.partner_line: Will the outdoor concert go ahead on Friday?
nodes.translation: ¿Se hará el concierto al aire libre el viernes?

options.text: It is almost certain, as long as the weather holds.
It is quite likely, but we have a backup plan.
It is hard to say yet; the forecast is not clear.

nodes.partner_line: Do you think the guest speaker will arrive on time?
nodes.translation: ¿Crees que el orador invitado llegará a tiempo?
nodes.model_reply: She is likely to arrive on time.

nodes.partner_line: What happens if the road to the venue is closed?
nodes.translation: ¿Qué pasa si cierran la carretera al lugar del evento?

options.text: In that case, we will move everyone by boat.
It is unlikely, but we have a contingency plan.
If that happens, the session will probably be postponed.
Almost, but one session might still change.
Not yet. It is likely to be confirmed tomorrow.

nodes.partner_line: How sure are you that the sponsors will attend?
nodes.translation: ¿Qué tan seguro estás de que los patrocinadores asistirán?

options.text: I am fairly sure. Three of them have already confirmed.
It is highly probable, though not guaranteed.
I would not say it is certain, but it looks promising.

nodes.partner_line: Thanks. Keep me updated if anything changes.
nodes.translation: Gracias. Mantenme informado si algo cambia.

options.text: Of course. I will let you know as soon as I hear anything.
Certainly. You will be the first to know.
Will do. I will send you a message this afternoon.
